assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amination into a general, ligand-tunable tool used from medicinal chemistry to materials; the ligand-design logic and breadth of use are clear, lasting and original beyond the earlier Pd cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the decisive general catalyst systems independently and are the natural pair; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling was a precursor but the broad practical method is theirs.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation, industrial adoption and mechanistic understanding; recognition is fully mature and, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize may be argued by some members.
I rely on memory for the precise priority chronology between Kosugi, Buchwald and Hartwig.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened a new mode of radical reactivity under mild conditions and is now a general platform in synthesis, including in industry; it enables a whole community in the sense I value.
assessment.attribution: Yoon, Stephenson and MacMillan reported the founding synthetic demonstrations around 2008-2009; Nicewicz, Konig, Melchiorre and Fukuzumi made major contributions, so any trio leaves out important work. MacMillan is already a laureate, which the committee may weigh.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced and applied, with extensive mechanistic study; still developing but already mature as a field.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse and a three-person cut is contestable.
Prior laureate status of one proposed person may weigh against.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts with controlled pores and active sites links crystal structure directly to function and underpins refining, petrochemicals and emissions control; structure-directing agents and new frameworks were solved with crystallographic evidence.
assessment.attribution: Davis, Corma and Zones represent design of frameworks, catalytic function and structure-directing agents; Tsapatsis and Yu also contributed (nanosheets, new open frameworks). I flag that this is my own field, so I judge it cautiously.
assessment.maturity: Long-established and commercially validated; timing is not premature, though the chemistry is spread over decades with no single sharp breakthrough.
uncertainties: Diffuse breakthrough moment makes a compact citation hard.
My field proximity may bias me; I am relying on memory about the individual contributions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allows structures of nanocrystals before radiation damage and time-resolved structural chemistry; as a structural method for crystals too small for ordinary X-ray work it resonates strongly with my own area.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu conceived diffraction-before-destruction, Chapman led the first demonstrations and methods, and Fromme drove the membrane-protein nanocrystal work; Schlichting made major time-resolved contributions, so the allocation is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced at several XFELs and used for time-resolved studies, but a limited number of facilities and a still-maturing set of chemical discoveries.
uncertainties: Whether the chemistry (as opposed to biology and instrumentation) is central to a chemistry prize.
Competing claims on credit among Chapman, Hajdu, Fromme and Schlichting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a spectacular rise in solar-cell efficiency and a new family of defect-tolerant semiconductors; originality and impact on energy materials are high.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites in cells, Park and Snaith drove the solid-state efficiency jump; Kanatzidis, Seok and Gratzel have major claims, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is well confirmed, but long-term stability, toxicity and device lifetime remain unresolved, which weighs against timeliness.
uncertainties: Operational stability not yet demonstrated at commercial scale.
Credit ordering among several strong contributors is disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides with tunable composition, giving broad functions in energy storage and electromagnetic applications; the structural and compositional design logic is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum made the first discovery (2011) and led the family's development; this triple is clean and well supported.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced, with a large community, though practical applications are still emerging and a few structural features, such as surface terminations, remain only partly resolved.
uncertainties: Surface termination structure and stability are not fully established.
Applications may not yet be sufficiently demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Template-directed ordered mesoporous silica introduced pore sizes beyond zeolites through surfactant self-assembly and opened a broad class of ordered porous solids; I know the field and its crystallographic characterization well.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck led the Mobil discovery of M41S; Inagaki (with Kuroda) reported FSM-16 independently; Zhao, Stucky and Ryoo extended it, so priority and extension credit are split.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed; the timing question is whether the impact has been surpassed by later porous materials, which have already been recognised in the prize system.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently recognised framework materials may reduce appeal.
Priority between the Mobil and Japanese groups needs checking beyond my memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The crystal structures of nitrogenase and their mechanistic follow-up address how biology reduces dinitrogen, a central problem in bioinorganic chemistry, with strong structural evidence for the cofactor, including the central carbide.
assessment.attribution: Rees and Einsle determined and refined the key cofactor structures; Dean, Seefeldt and Ribbe contributed biochemical and mechanistic work, so the group boundary is unclear.
assessment.maturity: The structures are well established, but the actual catalytic mechanism and intermediates are still debated, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of substrate binding and reduction remains unresolved.
Contributions of the biochemistry groups are difficult to separate from the structures.
